t: A multicenter registry suggested that esmolol infusions may benefit a subset of TTS patients who develop acute left ventricular outflow tract obstruction by reducing systemic blood pressure and intraventricular pressure gradients.

A study examining CSF from a large cohort of Long COVID patients found no observable Alzheimer's disease-related pathology, suggesting cognitive impairment in Long COVID may be mechanistically distinct from AD, at least in the months to years following infection.

GSK3β expression weakly induces neurite elongation and NGF-induced Lhx8/ChAT expression, an effect enhanced by WNK1 and HSN2 but suppressed by HSN2-delA and HSN2-insT mutants, which also increase Gad1 expression.
In severe COVID-19, antibodies induce procoagulant platelets that expose membrane phospholipids, creating a catalytic surface intensifying thrombin production and contributing to elevated D-dimer.
A group of antigen-recognition genes (CD1E, FCRL3, FcGR, NODs, TLR4, and HLA subclasses) has been implicated as one genetic pillar contributing to GBS susceptibility.

Clinical experience suggests patients with POTS experience a significant reduction in various autonomic symptoms with implementation of a gluten-free diet, which may be an effective non-pharmacologic option in pregnancy.
A cluster of genes involved in antigen identification, processing, and presentation (CD1E, FCRL3, FcGR, NODs, TLR4, HLA subclasses) has been implicated in genetic susceptibility to GBS.
CSF biomarkers of amyloid and tau co-pathology showed no significant baseline stage-based separation and no significant difference in longitudinal change at the group level.
PPH after breakfast was positively associated with the morning BP surge observed on ABPM, complicating intensive BP control based on early-morning home BP readings taken before breakfast.

Compared with healthy controls, POTS patients showed higher somatic vigilance and anxiety and increased anticipatory tachycardia before tilt-table upright positioning, an indicator of implicit fear conditioning.

In stroke-in-evolution cases, HRV complexity index values are significantly lower, whereas higher values are associated with reduced risk of stroke-in-evolution, suggesting HRV as an early warning marker of worsening neurological status.
Dos Santos et al. reported less reactive hyperemia in diabetic patients with and without CAN compared to healthy subjects, with higher resting heart rate in those with CAN.
Disruption of sympathetic innervation to the spleen after SCI results in splenic atrophy and impaired lymphocyte function, reducing the capacity to mount effective immune responses.

Schwann cell-derived exosomes containing MFG-E8 shift macrophage/microglia polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype via the SOCS3/STAT3 pathway, reducing inflammation after SCI; knockout of MFG-E8 in Schwann cells reversed this anti-inflammatory effect.
Studies report platelet hyperactivation and fibrin amyloid microclots resistant to breakdown in ME/CFS, potentially obstructing blood flow and limiting oxygen delivery.
In a rat model, COX blockade attenuated the rise in blood pressure seen with venous distension, supporting pharmacological modulation of VDR.

Patients with dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency cannot convert dopamine to norepinephrine/epinephrine and present with orthostatic hypotension, but they are able to maintain their BP after meals, unlike typical PPH patients.

Studies have found evidence of persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection, antigen reservoirs, and oral and intestinal dysbiosis in subsets of LC patients, linked to gastrointestinal symptoms and elevated risk of developing LC.
TadCBEd-SpRY combined with gRNA-C11 achieved efficient on-target correction of the ELP1 T6C mutation without any bystander editing.
ChAT knockout in sympathetic neurons abolished the post-MI increase in cardiac acetylcholine while norepinephrine levels remained unchanged, and reduced myocardial infarction severity.

FD mice exhibited swelling of the middle retinal layers (IPL/INL/OPL) and thinning of the outer retina, a novel structural abnormality potentially linked to retinal inflammation such as reactive astrogliosis and microglial activation reported previously in this model and in post-mortem FD patient retinae.

CSF levels of SERPINA3-encoded alpha-1-antichymotrypsin were higher in MSA patients, correlating with greater AA genotype distribution and with earlier onset and faster disease progression compared to non-AA genotypes.

Increased blood pressure variability in PSP was suggested to influence executive function, possibly via altered cerebral perfusion, though this preliminary finding requires replication and neuroimaging support to establish causality.
IDENTIFY-HF study found arterial stiffness progressively increases with vascular comorbidity burden, with HFpEF patients showing the highest levels and HFrEF patients showing near-normal stiffness.
FHOD3, which regulates actin filament assembly in cardiomyocyte sarcomeres and has mutations linked to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, showed differential methylation in OH patients.
Neuron-specific deletion of Elp1 caused reduced E-cadherin expression in the colon epithelium.

Biallelic pathogenic DST variants were previously known to cause hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI via loss of the DST-a isoform, and epidermolysis bullosa simplex 3 via loss of the DST-e isoform.
SPECT imaging in acute TTS showed increased cerebral blood flow in the basal ganglia, brainstem and hippocampus, with a decrease in prefrontal cortex flow.

Cognitive dysfunction ('brain fog') with mild-to-moderate impairment and depression on neuropsychological testing occurs in POTS patients, possibly due to catecholamine pathway dysfunction or brain structural abnormalities.

iNOS, an enzyme generating reactive nitrogen species contributing to inflammation and ARDS, is proposed alongside CB1 inhibition as a combined theoretical target to reduce inflammation and fibrosis in heart, lungs, and kidneys in post-COVID condition.
ICC dysfunction in diabetes is driven by increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and reduced antioxidant-supporting macrophage activity.

CNS symptoms such as headache, fatigue, chronic dizziness, cognitive dysfunction and sleep disturbance affect a large proportion of POTS patients and are often more disabling than orthostatic tachycardia itself.

ATP depletion during hypoglycaemia impairs Na+/K+ pump function, raising intracellular sodium, reducing action potential upstroke velocity and conduction velocity, and via NCX reversal and Ca2+ overload contributes to bradycardia and AV block.
Neuroimaging studies found hypoactivity in the insula, thalamus, and limbic cortex, suggesting cortical-limbic disconnection contributes to ME/CFS symptoms.

Right insular lesions increase sympathetic tone causing tachycardia and arrhythmias, while left insular lesions increase parasympathetic activity causing bradycardia, hypotension, and reduced HRV, raising cardiac death risk after stroke.

Prior literature cited in this paper reports that LAMB4 downregulation is associated with sporadic diverticulitis, a peripheral neuropathy of enteric neurons caused by reduced neuronal density of NCC-derived enteric neurons.
Pro-inflammatory cytokines act on central autonomic regulatory centers to increase sympathetic outflow and reduce parasympathetic tone, lowering heart rate variability and raising arrhythmic risk.
A two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis found that genetic susceptibility to COVID-19 was not associated with risk or progression of Alzheimer's disease.

Detection of α1AR autoantibodies in POTS patients was accompanied by significant elevation of several cytokines compared to control subjects, suggesting an autoinflammatory component alongside autoimmunity in POTS.
The Gastrointestinal function index of COMPASS-31 worsened acutely, improved by 1 and 3 months, then worsened again at 6 and 12 months.

Children with higher baseline erythrocytic H2S production (>27.1 nmol/(min·10^8 RBC)) showed greater long-term symptom improvement and higher symptom-free survival after midodrine hydrochloride treatment than those with lower baseline H2S.

Abdominal compression is preferred over lower-leg compression because it can be inflated to the minimum effective pressure to support blood pressure without the circulation disturbance risk associated with lower-leg compression.

Prior SARS-CoV-2 infection history could not be directly linked to POTS diagnosis in the original study because PCR test records were inaccessible due to Ministry of Health confidentiality regulations during the pandemic.
SNRIs such as duloxetine, venlafaxine, and milnacipran have demonstrated efficacy in reducing pain in fibromyalgia, musculoskeletal conditions, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

Because patients with neurodegenerative synucleinopathies are generally frail and at high risk of falls, overly aggressive blood pressure targets should be avoided and treatment goals individualized when managing nSH.
Physical functioning scores worsened acutely, improved by 1 and 3 months, then worsened again at 6 and 12 months.

The authors conclude that autonomic nervous system dysfunction contributes to the pathophysiology of CSCR and that automated pupillometry could serve as a non-invasive screening tool for detecting autonomic dysfunction in this disease.
Both alpha-synuclein and the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein bind toll-like receptor 4, activating transcription factors that induce proinflammatory cytokines and interferons.

Differential methylation was found in the lipoxygenase-related genes ALOX15 and LOXHD1, which convert polyunsaturated fatty acids into bioactive lipid mediators, suggesting altered catabolic/lipid metabolism in OH patients with reduced activity.
Bryarly et al. found very low and low levels of gACh autoantibodies in both POTS patients and controls with no clinical difference between seropositive and seronegative POTS patients.

The child presented with a multisystem clinical phenotype including corneal opacity/scarring, absent corneal reflex, missing front teeth, dry skin with anhidrosis, absent lacrimation during crying, recurrent unexplained fevers, multiple self-mutilation scars/ulcers, and shortening of distal phalanges.

Contrasting earlier claims, prior research suggested that cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction and microalbuminuria are related to each other but neither independently predicts cardiovascular mortality, possibly due to methodological limitations in scoring systems.
Fatigue scores worsened acutely, improved by 1 and 3 months, then worsened again at 6 and 12 months.

Coagulopathy is equally or more prevalent in patients with isolated TBI compared to those with concurrent injuries, even though isolated TBI patients experience less blood loss and receive less fluid resuscitation.
Combined siRNA knockdown of Wnk1 and Wnk4 suppresses NGF-mediated neurite elongation and Lhx8/ChAT expression while inducing Gad1 in Neuro2A cells, more strongly than knockdown of either alone.
Sustained catecholamine elevation causes persistent tachycardia, increased myocardial oxygen demand, and increased cardiac excitability, initially adaptive but becoming arrhythmogenic over time.
Hereditary alpha-tryptasemia, as a natural overexpression model of alpha-tryptase, has raised the potential of tryptase genotyping as a genetic biomarker for anaphylaxis severity.
Pain scores worsened acutely, improved by 1 and 3 months, then worsened again at 6 and 12 months.
The Orthostatic Intolerance domain of COMPASS-31 worsened acutely after COVID-19, improved by 1 and 3 months, then worsened again at 6 and 12 months.
COMPASS-31 total autonomic symptom score worsened at hospital discharge compared to pre-infection baseline, improved through 1 and 3 months, but then unexpectedly worsened again at 6 and 12 months.

In a 6-month open-label RCT of T2DM patients with distal peripheral neuropathy, dapagliflozin added to standard therapy significantly improved corneal nerve fiber density, branch density, and length, whereas intraepidermal nerve fiber density increased similarly in both treatment arms.

Management of multiple system atrophy is symptomatic, addressing parkinsonism, ataxia, autonomic dysfunction, and other motor/nonmotor symptoms via a multidisciplinary, multisystem approach including palliative care.

Daily ambulatory monitoring of World Trade Center responders revealed that increases in PTSD symptoms were associated with concurrent decreases in heart rate variability, suggesting moment-to-moment coupling between psychological distress and autonomic control.
A phase 2 trial of lithium in MSA patients was terminated after interim analysis revealed severe adverse effects, indicating poor tolerability.

Applying an external neck collar to compress the carotid body and sinus reduced orthostatic symptoms and resting ventilation, both at baseline and during head-up tilt, in POTS patients, along with improvement in the chest discomfort component of the Vanderbilt POTS Symptom Score.

Electron microscopy of the Tecpr2 ki/ki medulla showed myelinated axons with attenuated myelin sheaths filled with swollen mitochondria, enlarged ER, lysosomes, single-membrane vesicles, autophagosomes, glycogen granules, and amorphous protein aggregates.
GBS following COVID-19 has been identified as a postinfectious immune-mediated process that responds to IVIG or plasmapheresis.

Pyridostigmine, a reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, amplifies residual sympathetic outflow to preferentially raise upright blood pressure with lower risk of supine hypertension, but is limited by GI adverse effects.
Compression stockings, exercise, diet, or medications aimed at improving arterial elasticity may enhance blood distribution during standing and reduce reflex tachycardia in POTS.
COVID-19 vaccination did not reduce the overall risk of developing most long COVID features, though fatigue and myalgia were less common in vaccinated individuals.
Optical coherence tomography failed to demonstrate ruptured plaques or intracoronary thrombi in the LAD, suggesting plaque rupture is unlikely the primary TTS mechanism.

Successful catheter ablation for AF was accompanied by partial normalization of specific gut microbial taxa and circulating metabolomic profiles, suggesting a bidirectional relationship between rhythm-control interventions and the gut-heart axis.

One study showed insufficient ATP synthesis specifically by mitochondrial complex V, alongside elevated function of complexes I-IV and TORC1 activity, suggesting a compensatory mechanism insufficient for increased energy demand such as during exercise.
Dobutamine stress echocardiogram showed an exaggerated heart rate response to exercise and below average functional capacity, without evidence of ischemia or angina.

T2DM is linked to irregularities in innate and adaptive immune responses, including reduced cytokine production, impaired phagocytic activity, unregulated immune cell responses and diminished capacity to eliminate microbial pathogens.

A 2025 cohort study found that in ACS patients, life stressors in the presence of suicidal ideation at two weeks post-event were associated with poorer long-term major adverse cardiac outcomes, supporting early psychosocial assessment after ACS.
Interferon signaling and response GO terms were strongly positively enriched across almost all identified cell types in vagus nerve, including neurons and endothelial cells, in COVID-19.

Several anticancer treatments—anthracyclines, taxanes, vinca-alkaloids, platinum-based agents, head and neck radiotherapy, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation—have been linked to the development of autonomic dysfunction, alongside contributing factors such as psychological stress, sleep disturbances, weight gain, and loss of cardiorespiratory fitness.
A phase 2 trial of lithium in MSA patients was terminated due to severe adverse effects identified at interim analysis, indicating lithium was not well tolerated in this population.

Nissl staining showed cardiac arrest-induced neuronal loss and Nissl body depletion in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus that was amplified by sleep deprivation and partially preserved by electroacupuncture.
Measuring blood lactate levels has been proposed as a digital/biochemical marker to detect the risk of developing more severe post-exertional malaise in ME/CFS.

Total peripheral resistance (TPR) may actually increase during long-duration missions as a compensatory mechanism to maintain blood pressure despite reduced circulating volume, contrary to earlier assumptions of reduced TPR.

The authors acknowledge that small fiber neuropathy and autoimmune/autonomic dysfunction triggered by viral infections such as SARS-CoV-2 may contribute to POTS pathophysiology, though this could not be directly assessed due to lack of access to diagnostic tools (skin biopsy, corneal confocal microscopy, Sudoscan) at their center.

Breathing pattern disorders are very frequently seen in autonomic dysfunction, with overlap among conditions including PoTS/orthostatic intolerance, inappropriate sinus tachycardia, chronic fatigue syndrome and post-acute COVID syndrome.

Chronic CSCR can lead to RPE degeneration and secondary choroidal neovascular membranes requiring anti-VEGF injections, with half-fluence photodynamic therapy (Visudyne) and focal laser treatment cited as proven options that remodel pachychoroid vasculature.

VM patients show grey matter morphological networks that are more locally clustered yet less efficiently connected, particularly in the left superior temporal gyrus, and machine learning could differentiate VM from healthy participants using these features.

Protein aggregates in Dst-b mutant skeletal muscle were composed of a variety of proteins including αB-crystallin, plectin, myotilin, and truncated Dst-b protein, similar to composition of aggregates in other myofibrillar myopathies.
By E12.5, the frontal (ophthalmic) nerve showed decreased branching complexity in Elp1 CKO embryos compared to Control, as quantified by modified Sholl analysis.

Vagus nerve stimulation may exert anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting pro-inflammatory cytokine release and modulating sympathetic excitation, suggesting a potential therapeutic approach for autonomic dysfunction in COVID-19.

Elp1 binds to phosphorylated TrkA/Shp1 complexes in retrogradely transported signaling endosomes and represses Shp1 (PTPN6) phosphatase activity, maintaining TrkA phosphorylation during its retrograde transport from axon terminals to the neuronal nucleus to sustain NGF-dependent differentiation and survival signaling.

Concerns about complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) following HPV vaccination led to decreased public confidence, decreased coverage rates, and/or withdrawal of national HPV vaccination recommendations in countries including Japan, Denmark and Ireland.

Histology of the lacrimal gland after CUMS modeling showed increased interstitial space, lax glandular structure, dilated ducts, fluid accumulation in acinar cells, and disorganized acinar cell structure compared to controls.
Serum from ALS patients with SPTLC1 variants did not show elevated deoxysphingolipids but instead showed increased free sphinganine and circulating ceramide levels compared to controls.

Patients with otolith dysfunction had a higher incidence of orthostatic hypotension during active standing compared to those with normal cervical vestibular-evoked myogenic potentials, suggesting otolith dysfunction may induce OH.
A 'bacterial contamination hypothesis' proposes microbes contribute to endometriosis pathology via inflammatory responses involving TLR4 and TLR2 activation.

Patients with POTS after either vaccination or infection were managed with standard-of-care therapies including salt tablets, hydration, structured exercise, compression stockings, beta blockers, ivabradine, midodrine, and clonidine (for hyperadrenergic variants), and appeared to respond to conventional therapy.
Autoantibodies targeting specific nervous system components have been identified in a subset of CRPS patients, supporting an autoimmune contribution to persistent inflammation and neuronal damage.

Semmes-Weinstein monofilament testing is the preferred practical point-of-care test for peripheral nerve tactile threshold monitoring, but thermal (heat-detection) tests may reveal abnormalities earlier and monofilament testing is less sensitive than nerve conduction studies/EMG for early detection of neural abnormalities.
Initial management of POTS/OH is generally non-pharmacological, including trigger avoidance, graded exercise training, waist-high compression stockings, and liberal salt and fluid intake.
The INOVATE-HF trial found no evidence that vagus nerve stimulation reduced mortality or cardiovascular events in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
Beta-blockers reduced heart rate and alleviated palpitations and tremors but may worsen symptoms in patients with low blood pressure.

In MPTP-injected mice, phosphorylated α-syn accumulated in Schwann cells of the vagus nerve and interacted with Toll-like receptors to induce apoptosis, leading to gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and urinary autonomic dysfunction.

Levels of endogenous NO, H2S, sulfur dioxide, serum copeptin, and CNP differed significantly between children with POTS and controls, implicating vasoactive signaling molecules in peripheral vascular dysfunction.

The NOD2 rs3135500 variant, which activates NF-κB-mediated inflammation, was associated with increased MSA risk and correlated with higher peripheral mononuclear cell NOD2 mRNA and plasma protein levels.
Nearly all studies reported increased cardiac output following counter pressure maneuvers, likely driven by increased stroke volume rather than heart rate.
Holmes-Adie syndrome, a rare autonomic dysfunction disorder affecting cranial (including vagal) nerves, presents with tonic pupils, areflexia, patchy anhidrosis/hyperhidrosis, and chronic cough.

A clinical trial comparing healthy controls to patients with bladder/pelvic pain syndromes using autonomic testing demonstrated that these patients can experience orthostatic intolerance due to autonomic neuropathy.

Joint and connective tissue laxity in females may fluctuate with hormones, especially estradiol, throughout the menstrual cycle, raising the question of whether this is exacerbated in Long COVID patients with connective tissue disorders.
In a bedrest study, restoring plasma volume with intravenous isotonic fluids and oral salt improved presyncope/syncope after bedrest, but volume loading did not prevent orthostatic tachycardia.
Michl et al. (2011) found significantly higher ranunculin levels in Ranunculus repens samples from EGS-associated pastures compared with control pastures.

Polyradiculoneuropathy, including Guillain-Barre syndrome and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, is described as the most severe form of peripheral neuropathy irAE, causing significant muscle weakness.
dSA (but not sphingosine) induced ubiquitination of SK1, similar to known substrate-based SK1 inhibitors PF543 and SKi-II.

Alternate orthostatic definitions using a DBP drop ≥5 mm Hg (for orthostatic hypotension) and DBP rise ≥15 mm Hg (for orthostatic hypertension) were more strongly associated with adverse events than the traditional consensus thresholds.

Prior unimodal HRV literature cited in this study reports reduced parasympathetic vagal tone as a characteristic autonomic feature of MDD, hypothesized to relate to altered brain-level autonomic control.
The ELN gene, encoding elastin, has also been proposed as a candidate gene associated with hEDS/HSD, though inheritance shows no clear single genetic etiology.
Post-COVID patients exhibit reduced HDL cholesterol as part of an unfavorable lipid profile.
Both low- and high-intensity exercise can reduce pro-inflammatory cytokines, promote beneficial changes in gut microbiota, and improve health-related quality of life in IBD patients.
NaV-mediated inward current density correlates with the number of repetitively fired action potentials, linking channel expression level to firing phenotype (phasic vs tonic).

Postmortem examination of a COVID-19 patient revealed viral-like particles in the capillary endothelium of the frontal lobe with active budding across the endothelial basolateral membrane, supporting a hematogenous route of CNS entry via the blood-brain barrier.

Tg2576 mice, a model of cerebral amyloidosis, showed reduced cerebral and cardiac BDNF, associated with reduced cardiac sympathetic nerve fibre density; Aβ incubation of cardiomyocytes reduced BDNF and GAP-43 (a neuronal regeneration marker).
HSAN9 patient-derived fibroblasts, TECPR2-deficient mouse embryonic fibroblasts, and dorsal root ganglia neurons show severe mitochondrial dysfunction with accumulation of mitochondrial content.

The NOD2 rs3135500 variant, which activates NF-κB-mediated inflammation, was associated with increased MSA risk and correlated with increased peripheral mononuclear cell NOD2 mRNA and plasma NOD2 protein levels.
The tubulin acetylation defect in FD fibroblasts was not due to increased HDAC6 deacetylation activity nor intracellular protein aggregation.
Pyridostigmine does not appear to improve symptoms in slow-transit constipation but has demonstrated clinical benefit in recurrent intestinal pseudo-obstruction with a favorable safety profile.
Dysautonomia/orthostatic symptoms improved between initial PCoCC evaluation and follow-up survey.

Regular exercise, including strength training and cardiovascular exercise, improves fatigue, exercise intolerance, and quality of life in dysautonomia patients, especially those with orthostatic intolerance.

Cardioneuroablation, targeting fibrillar myocardium around the sinus and AV nodes, has been used to treat carotid sinus hypersensitivity and may be an alternative to pacemaker implantation, particularly in younger patients.

PD patients with symptomatic neurogenic orthostatic hypotension/postprandial hypotension and peripheral leg edema are often on diuretics despite receiving dopamine agonists and/or amantadine, which themselves can cause edema, so discontinuing/reducing these agents (compensated by increasing levodopa or adding MAO-B/COMT inhibitors) plus compression stockings is recommended.
Medicinal treatment strategies proposed for POTS include alpha-1 agonists, steroids, compression garments, and increased fluid and salt intake.
Pregabalin, a gabapentinoid used for GAD, carries risks of cardiac side effects and FDA-flagged respiratory depression, warranting caution in COVID-19 patients.

Treatment of HIV-associated orthostatic hypotension with autonomic dysfunction may include liberal fluids, NaCl supplementation, compression stockings, head-of-bed elevation, fludrocortisone, midodrine, or droxidopa.
Endothelial activation in the gastric wall of SSc patients was marked by upregulation of adhesion molecules VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and E-selectin, accompanied by perivascular CD4+ lymphocytic infiltration.

GBA mutations are associated with more severe motor decline and myotonia, and patients are more likely to experience non-motor symptoms including cognitive dysfunction, depression, olfactory disturbances, and RBD.

Acute SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with abnormal host immune responses to traumatized connective tissue and elevations in antinuclear antibodies linked to connective tissue disease in hypermobile patients.
The cholinergic anti-inflammatory reflex mediated by α7nAChR was proposed as a mechanism in the brain-kidney axis of DKD, though supported by very low-quality evidence.
Lower University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) scores were significantly associated with orthostatic hypotension cross-sectionally.

Following inciting trauma, release of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-α promotes vascular permeability and sensitizes peripheral nociceptors, leading to hyperalgesia and allodynia in CRPS.

Cardiac 123I-MIBG imaging can help distinguish PD from multiple system atrophy (MSA) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), since the latter two conditions show only modest reduction in cardiac MIBG uptake compared to PD despite greater sympathetic ganglion dysfunction.

Exploratory analysis found that bradykinesia/rigidity and postural instability/gait difficulty domains of UPDRS-III were most strongly linked with rest-activity rhythm, with worse scores associated with lower relative amplitude and higher intradaily variability.
TECPR2 acts as a molecular linker between Rab5 and SNX17, as Rab5 binding to SNX17 (assessed by GST pulldown) is reduced upon TECPR2 depletion.
Total CSF α-synuclein concentration is significantly decreased in PD and MSA patients compared to healthy controls and tauopathies (PSP, CBD).
In CKD patients with masked uncontrolled hypertension, nocturnal hypertension is highly prevalent and strongly associated with left ventricular hypertrophy and poor renal outcomes.
iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from TTS patients show enhanced β1-adrenergic receptor signaling and heightened catecholamine-dependent responses.
TNF-α/NF-κB signaling was identified as a core mechanism amplifying neuroinflammation along the brain-kidney axis in diabetic kidney disease, based primarily on preclinical evidence.
Carrying risk GBA mutations was significantly associated with orthostatic hypotension cross-sectionally.
Standardized nutritional screening, prokinetic agents, and small bowel or transpyloric feeding have shown benefits for symptomatic management and recovery of GI function after TBI.
Anti-inflammatory therapies (antihistamines, oral cromolyn, omalizumab) were used to treat suspected MCAS symptoms, with all treated patients reporting clinical improvement.
In a multicenter Japanese RCT, landiolol reduced heart rate in septic shock patients but did not significantly reduce mortality (a secondary endpoint).
The phase II SPARK trial of cinpanemab (BIIB054) was halted after the drug missed its primary and secondary endpoints in Parkinson's disease patients.
Higher RBD Screening Questionnaire (RBDSQ) scores were significantly associated with orthostatic hypotension cross-sectionally.

Ivabradine may be useful for tachycardia-related electrophysiology disorders such as inappropriate sinus tachycardia and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, though it has not gained wide acceptance for these uses.
Combining optimized potent oral kinetin derivatives with intrathecal ASOs and intravitreal gene therapy using viral vectors is proposed as a synergistic therapeutic approach to elevate ELP1 levels.

Gene Ontology analysis of downregulated genes in KO, FD1/KO, and FD9/KO embryos revealed enrichment for nervous system development pathways including synapse formation, neuron projection, and axon growth.

Autoimmune phenomena reported after COVID-19 vaccination include immune thrombocytopenic purpura, autoimmune liver diseases, Guillain-Barré syndrome, IgA nephropathy, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
FD symNs plated in compartmentalized culture devices with an NGF gradient showed impaired axon outgrowth, consistent with defective NGF retrograde transport reported previously.

Sympathetic denervation improved lacrimal gland histology (denser cellular architecture, reduced apoptosis, restored nuclear morphology) and reduced inflammatory cytokine expression compared with model and placebo groups.
In treatment-naive parkinsonism patients, the D1 agonist CY 208-243 significantly decreased supine blood pressure, heart rate, and norepinephrine and caused orthostatic hypotension.

Unlike controls, POTS patients show a significant rise in the LF component of HRV and muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) with standing and hypotension, indicating augmented sympathetic outflow following haemodynamic challenge.

The degree of gut dysbiosis after SCI correlates with injury severity and level, being more pronounced in complete than incomplete injuries and in cervical/high thoracic versus lower thoracic/lumbar lesions.

Exposure of brain endothelial cells to serum from long COVID patients induced expression of inflammatory markers and increased adhesion of peripheral blood mononuclear cells to brain endothelial cells in vitro.
Wearable activity and fitness trackers measuring step counts and energy expenditure are commonly used in both ME/CFS and FM to provide meaningful longitudinal disease-progression data.

AADC deficiency, caused by biallelic DDC variants, impairs conversion of L-DOPA to dopamine and 5-hydroxytryptophan to serotonin, causing combined deficiency of dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, and epinephrine with autonomic dysfunction as part of the phenotype.
Compared with the general population, women with the three most common types of EDS have higher rates of spontaneous abortions, miscarriages, stillbirths, and preterm premature rupture of membranes.
SOD1 mutations, common in familial ALS, cause protein misfolding, mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress, producing a rapidly progressive limb-onset phenotype with early respiratory failure.
Gastric wall endothelium in SSc shows upregulated adhesion molecules (VCAM-1, ICAM-1, E-selectin) with perivascular CD4+ lymphocytic infiltration, supporting sustained endothelial-immune interaction.
Patients with DM show lower rates of immediate cardioversion success and sinus rhythm maintenance, with glycemic control emerging as an independent predictor of treatment failure.

In HEK293 SPTLC1-knockout cells, the classic HSAN1 variant p.(C133W) increased de novo synthesis of 1-deoxyceramides, while ALS-associated SPTLC1 variants increased canonical SPT product levels instead.

Short-chain fatty acids, particularly butyrate, upregulate tight junctions, inhibit TLR4/NF-κB signaling, lower circulating LPS and pro-inflammatory cytokines, and regulate BBB permeability and microglial activation.

A sensitivity analysis excluding SCOPA-AUT items related to orthostatic symptoms (questions 14-18) did not materially alter the observed association between dysautonomia and motor/non-motor fluctuations, suggesting orthostatic hypotension alone does not explain the relationship.

Blood melatonin concentrations were reduced in Alzheimer's disease patients alongside defective ventricular contraction, and Aβ40/Aβ42 reduce pineal melatonin production and downregulate melatonin receptors on endothelial cells.
TRPV2 inhibition with tranilast prevented autonomic dysfunction in the SU5416/hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension rat model.
Studies in POTS patients showed inconsistent findings regarding whether both physical and mental health SF-36 summary scores are impaired, or only the physical component.

A Cochrane review of RCTs found limited evidence for fludrocortisone's efficacy in OH, with low/very low quality evidence, particularly regarding long-term use, due to short duration and small sample sizes of most trials.
POTS has been reported to be associated with several autoantibodies including antinuclear, antithyroid, anti-NMDA glutamate receptor, antiphospholipid, and Sjogren antibodies.
TRPV2 inhibition restored calcium homeostasis and attenuated remodeling of ion channels (Kv4.3, Kv4.2, Kv1.5, Kir3.1, Kir3.4, KCNK3) and connexins (Cx40, Cx43) in PH rat hearts.
Post-COVID endocrine dysfunction, including hypocortisolemia (low cortisol), thyroid dysfunction, and new-onset diabetes mellitus, has been identified in some PASC patients.
After vaccination, exercise-induced IFN-γ responses at 60% intensity were strongest for spike (and alpha-variant), followed by nucleocapsid, then membrane protein.
In SMN2-targeting U1 snRNA-treated samples, a considerably heavier band appeared that Sanger sequencing suggested was an intron retention product, occurring to varying degrees across the ten guides.

Paediatric dysautonomia is conceptualised as a distributed brain-heart-vascular network disorder requiring standardised orthostatic assessment and exclusion of structural heart disease and arrhythmia, rather than a primary cardiac condition.
Higher HRV is associated with improved emotion regulation and reduced anxiety and rumination.

The myocarditis safety signal following mRNA vaccination only became apparent once analyses were stratified by age and sex, revealing a sharp excess among young men that had been obscured in aggregate population-level analyses.

In rodent models, insulin-induced severe hypoglycaemia produced marked catecholamine surges, QT prolongation, and lethal arrhythmias that were significantly attenuated by adrenergic blockade or adrenalectomy.

Menstrual cycle hormones affect hemodynamics (cardiac output, stroke volume, total peripheral resistance) in POTS patients but not in healthy controls, possibly via renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system modulation.
A longitudinal cohort found that all autonomic symptoms except pupillary movement were more severe and deteriorated more rapidly in PD patients with RBD than without RBD.

Menstrual cycle hormones influence hemodynamic measures such as cardiac output, stroke volume, and total peripheral resistance in POTS patients, an effect not observed in healthy controls, possibly through modulation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.

Gibbons et al. reported that participants with POTS and comorbid hypermobile EDS showed both improvement and minimal adverse effects with the exercise protocol, suggesting exercise may be safe and tolerable in this subgroup.
The 1H7 and 5C1 antibodies decreased toxic truncated alpha-synuclein species, improved behavioral deficits and protected tyrosine hydroxylase-positive cells in Thy1-alpha-synuclein transgenic mice.

Post-TBI gastrointestinal dysfunction is proposed to arise primarily from autonomic dysfunction, increased intracranial pressure, and systemic inflammation, leading to intestinal dysmotility and malabsorption.

Oral sodium butyrate supplementation significantly reduced myocardial infarct size after ischemia/reperfusion compared with untreated I/R rats, and this protective effect was diminished by subdiaphragmatic vagotomy.

A systematic review and meta-analysis found significantly lower serum B12 and holotranscobalamin, and elevated homocysteine and methylmalonic acid, in vegans compared to omnivores, indicating both low and functional B12 deficiency; supplementation significantly improved all biomarkers in vegans.
Transcutaneous magnetic stimulation failed to demonstrate superiority over sham treatment for diabetic neuropathy pain.

Patients with CKD have altered resting brachial artery shear patterns compared with age-matched controls, which likely contributes to CKD-related endothelial dysfunction assessed by flow-mediated dilation.
Cognitive impairment ('brain fog') in POTS patients may be caused by dysfunction of the catecholamine pathway and related brain structures.

Spinal nociceptive-specific neurons in Fam134b/cdKO mice showed markedly increased firing rate, burst frequency, and duration of excitation compared with WT, with a milder increase in Fam134cKO alone and no change in Fam134bKO alone.

Sciatic/tibial nerve of Fam134b/cdKO mice showed progressive axonal degeneration, mild at 4 weeks with accumulation of smaller axons, and massive loss of axons (especially larger ones) by 15 weeks, with collagen replacing degenerated axon area on EM.

Axonal ER in Fam134b/cdKO sciatic nerve accumulated abnormal ladder-like/transverse ER tubules (instead of normal longitudinal tubules), with ~75% of axons showing intermediate or accumulated ER phenotype already at 4 weeks, preceding overt degeneration.
Fam134b/cdKO mice had a markedly shortened lifespan, never surviving past 25 weeks, unlike other genotypes.
